Subject: Post-incident update: root cause and immediate remediation actions

Daniel / Tessa — quick technical summary and actions taken so far. Keeping it tight so you can share with ops.

What we observed
- At 07:46 PT a small deployment that touched the quota-mapping service introduced a config regression: a stale mapping file was re-applied to a subset of tenants. That mapping incorrectly associated several Nova Health tenant ids with a lower quota tier.
- Result: token-bucket limits for affected tenants were reduced to the lower tier (approx 10 rps equivalent) causing the 429 spike during normal traffic bursts.
- The serving runtime returned 429s with the message "quota exceeded for tenant" (matches your capture).

Immediate remediation (completed at 08:18 PT)
- Rolled back the quota-mapping deployment and re-applied the correct mapping for nh-prod-01 and nh-prod-03.
- Temporarily increased burst window for the affected tenants to absorb backlog while rollback propagated.
- Cleared transient KV cache for the mapping service to avoid stale reads.

Follow-up actions (in flight)
- Root-cause fix: We've created a validation gate in the mapping CI to prevent stale files from being deployed (PR opened: INF-8243).
- Backfill: We'll recompute the quota usage and time-series for affected windows and provide you with a sanitized CSV.
- Postmortem: Drafting a one-page incident timeline and corrective actions (attached).
- Customer remediation: We're proposing a 10% service credit for the impacted billing window and three months of elevated monitoring for Nova Health at no cost while validation gates complete.

Attachments: incident_timeline.md, quota_mapping_diff.patch

Request for you
- Can you confirm which specific request-ids you still have from the 07:45–08:05 window? Those help us make direct trace correlations.

Sorry again for the disruption — we'll follow up with the formal postmortem and the backfilled metrics.

— Monica Patel
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
